brief: Runs a loop that ticks timers every few milliseconds, drains pending HTTP requests and stops when there is nothing left to do.
detail: Add started timers with AddTimer and call RunLoop. Each pass ticks every timer, drops the finished one-shots, drains the pending asynchronous requests of the stzReactiveHttp you hand in, advances detached timers and waits SetCheckFrequency milliseconds, on a real timer of the reactor if SetReactor gave one and a sleep otherwise. The loop ends when no timer remains and the patience, a count of idle passes, is used up, or when Stop is called. The manager keeps copies of its timers, so a callback stopping its own copy does not stop the manager's, and a loop with a repeating timer runs until the manager itself is stopped.
receiver:
$nFired = 0
oEngine = new stzReactive()
o1 = new stzTimerManager()
o1.SetCheckFrequency(5)
o2 = new stzReactiveTimer("first", 20, func { $nFired += 1 }, oEngine, 1)
o3 = new stzReactiveTimer("second", 40, func { $nFired += 10 }, oEngine, 1)
o2.Start()
o3.Start()
o1.AddTimer(o2)
o1.AddTimer(o3)
